 Advertisement Getty Images Khaled Mahmoud 1 hour ago Bayern player ratings vs Koln: Nathaniel Brown scores but the German giants frustrated by injury to Harry Kane
 Share Follow GOAL on Google Bayern Munich were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Koln at the Allianz Arena, a result overshadowed by a significant injury to Harry Kane. Despite dominating possession, the hosts struggled to convert their numerical superiority into goals after Nathaniel Brown's equaliser.
 Advertisement Bayern Munich’s tactical blueprint was thrown into disarray early at the Allianz Arena as Kane was forced off with a leg injury just 20 minutes into the contest. This unexpected pivot forced the Rekordmeister to operate without their primary reference point against a compact Koln block. The visitors had stunned the home crowd in the 12th minute when Mikey Moore clinical finished a fast break, exploiting a rare lapse in Bayern's defensive transition.
 The recovery was led by Brown, who restored parity in the 37th minute with a well-taken strike from outside the box. Despite controlling 71% of the ball and completing a staggering 747 accurate passes, Bayern lacked the final-third ingenuity to break down the Billy Goats' 3-5-1-1 structure. Koln actually finished the match with a higher Expected Goals (xG) value of 1.98 compared to Bayern's 0.94, suggesting that while the hosts held the ball, the visitors held the real threat.
 Goalkeeper & Defence
 Jonas Urbig - 7/10
 Urbig was largely a spectator for long periods due to Bayern's possession dominance, but he stood tall when required. He produced three vital saves. He could do little about Moore's opener which was a high-quality transition goal.
 Konrad Laimer - 6/10
 Occupying the right-back role, Laimer was an auxiliary midfielder for much of the game, pushing high to support Michael Olise. He registered two shots, both of which missed the target, and struggled at times to track back during Koln's lightning-fast counter-attacks.
 Advertisement Advertisement Jonathan Tah - 6/10
 Tah acted as the primary distributor from the back, helping recycle possession as Bayern probed for openings. He was generally secure but part of a defensive unit that looked vulnerable whenever Moore found space to run into.

 Dayot Upamecano - 7/10
 Statistically Bayern's best defender, Upamecano recorded 9 defensive interventions, including 2 tackles and 5 duels won. He nearly gave Bayern the lead with a powerful header in first-half stoppage time that forced a save. He was substituted in the 70th minute for Kim Min-Jae.
 Josip Stanisic - 6/10
 Stanisic provided a steady presence on the left of the defensive structure but lacked the overlapping dynamism often required to break down a low block. His role was more about containment and facilitating the build-up play.
 Advertisement Midfield
 Joshua Kimmich - 8/10
 The metronome of the side, Kimmich completed 131 accurate passes from 136 attempts, a staggering 96% success rate. He dictated the tempo and attempted to unlock the defence with long-range efforts, though his 22nd-minute shot failed to test the keeper.
 Aleksandar Pavlovic - 7/10
 Pavlovic worked tirelessly in the engine room, providing the platform for the more advanced players. He showed flashes of offensive intent with two blocked shots but his primary contribution was ensuring Bayern maintained their 71% share of possession before being replaced late on.
 Advertisement Michael Olise - 5/10
 A disappointing outing for the Frenchman, who struggled to exert his usual influence on the right wing. He saw one shot blocked in the 41st minute and failed to create any big chances before being forced off through injury at half-time for Tim Binder.
 Lennart Karl - 7/10
 Operating in the number ten role, Karl was Bayern's most frequent shooter, racking up 3 attempts. He forced a save in the 54th minute and was central to the team's creative efforts, though he found the Koln central trio difficult to bypass.
 Advertisement Nathaniel Brown - 8/10
 The standout performer in the attacking quartet. Brown showed excellent technique to score the equaliser in the 37th minute with a 22-metre strike. He remained a threat throughout, registering two additional shots and consistently testing the Koln full-backs.
 Attack
 Harry Kane - 5/10
 An evening that ended in heartbreak for the England captain. Before his 20th-minute exit due to a leg injury, Kane had very little service to work with as Bayern were still settling into their rhythm. His absence was felt acutely for the remainder of the match.
 Advertisement Substitutes & Manager
 Tom Bischof - 6/10
 Introduced early for the injured Kane, Bischof struggled to replicate the striker's gravity. He had two sights of goal, one blocked and one off target, but lacked the clinical edge required.
 Tim Binder - 6/10
 Came on at the interval for Olise. He offered a different profile on the flank but found the Koln defensive shape equally stubborn to penetrate.
 Advertisement Kim Min-Jae - 6/10
 A 70th-minute replacement for Upamecano, Kim brought fresh energy to the backline and helped snuff out late Koln breaks as the visitors looked for a winner.
 Jamal Musiala - 6/10
 Brought on for the final 20 minutes to provide some magic, Musiala had two late chances but couldn't find the target. His dribbling caused some chaos, yet the final ball was missing.
 Advertisement Noah Codjo-Evora - N/A
 A late cameo for Pavlovic, not enough time to impact the scoreline.
 Vincent Kompany - 6/10
 Kompany’s side dominated the ball but were tactically outmanoeuvred on the counter. The manager will be concerned by the lack of high-quality chances created (only 0.94 xG) despite having so much of the ball, and the injury to Kane now presents a significant structural challenge.
